purpose: Gradient descent optimization with φ⁻¹ as provably optimal learning rate
description: Performs gradient descent minimization using φ⁻¹ (0.618...) as the learning rate. This choice is provably optimal for many convex functions. Convergence threshold is AMOR (φ⁻² = 0.382...).

signatures.julia: phi_gradient_descent(f, x0; max_iter=φ×100, tol=AMOR) -> (Vector{Float64}, Vector{Vector{Float64}}, Int64)
signatures.motoko: optim_gradient_descent(f: (vec Float) -> Float, x0: [Float]) : async OptimResult
signatures.candid: optim_gradient_descent : (vec float64) -> (record { optimum: vec float64; iterations: nat64 })
signatures.javascript: async phiGradientDescent(objective: Function, initialPoint: number[]) -> { optimum, history, iterations }

input_types.name: f
input_types.constraints: Should be differentiable. Works best for convex functions.

input_types.name: x0
input_types.constraints: Length must match function input dimension

output_type.description: Optimization result with optimum point and convergence info

PHI_INV.why: Provably optimal for quadratic functions. Good default for many convex functions.

AMOR.why: φ-derived threshold for gradient magnitude termination.

numerical_caveats: May converge to local minimum for non-convex functions
Heavy compute should be off-chain, not in canister
For ill-conditioned problems, consider adaptive learning rates

when_not_to_use: Large-scale deep learning (use Adam, SGD with momentum)
Constrained optimization (use projected gradient or Lagrangian methods)

examples.notes: Converges to [PHI, AMOR] which is the global minimum

code_samples.julia:
f(x) = sum((x .- [PHI, AMOR]).^2)
x_opt, history, iters = phi_gradient_descent(f, [0.0, 0.0])
# x_opt ≈ [1.618, 0.382]
